# PART I: Foundations of LBBNN & Input-Skip Architecture (ISLaB)

## Motivation — Why Sparse & Explainable BNNs in Official Statistics?

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Black-Box \& Over-Parameterization Dilemma:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Modern deep neural networks capture complex multi-way interactions, but lack calibrated uncertainty quantification and interpretable feature attributions.
  \item Standard dense BNNs quantify parameter uncertainty, but retain all noise covariates, inflating variance in downstream survey estimators.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.5em}
\textbf{What Official Statistics Requires:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Structural Sparsity}: Combine model selection (spike-and-slab edge pruning) and parameter uncertainty in a single variational framework.
  \item \textbf{Explainable Depth}: Automatically adapt between simple linear GLMs ($\text{Depth} = 1$) and deep non-linear interaction surfaces ($\text{Depth} > 1$).
  \item \textbf{Survey \& Privacy Rigor}: Rigorous integration with informative sampling weights, differential privacy ($\epsilon, \delta$), and non-probability samples.
\end{itemize}

## From Dense BNNs to Latent Binary BNNs (Hubin & Storvik, 2024)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Spike-and-Slab Edge Selection:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Latent binary inclusion indicator $\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} \in \{0, 1\}$:
  \small
  $$p\big(w_{k,p}^{(j)} \mid \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\mathcal{N}\big(0, (\tau_{k,p}^{(j)})^2\big) + \big(1-\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)\delta_0$$
  $$p\big(\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \text{Bernoulli}\big(\psi_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA)}: Ensembles across posterior draws $\Gamma \sim q(\Gamma)$ and $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma)$ for optimal uncertainty quantification.
  \item \textbf{Median Probability Model (MPM)}: Hard-prunes edges with inclusion probability $\alpha_{k,p}^{(j)} \le 0.5$ (Barbieri \& Berger, 2004 optimal predictive submodel).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Input-Skip LBBNNs (ISLaB) & Structural Depth Metrics (Høyheim et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{The ISLaB Architecture (\textit{JAIR}, 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Direct skip connections route raw input covariates $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ to every hidden layer:
  $$\mathbf{a}^{(j-1)} = \left[a_1^{(j-1)}, \dots, a_K^{(j-1)}, \mathbf{x}^\top\right]^\top$$
  \item \textbf{Active Paths ($\text{AP}$)}: An active path connects input $x_k$ to output $\zeta$ if all intermediate edges have $\alpha_{k,p}^{(j)} > 0.5$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Contribution Depth Classification:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Depth = 1 (Linear Skip)}: Input-to-output skip $\implies$ linear GLM effect.
  \item \textbf{Depth $\ge$ 2 (Non-Linear)}: Through hidden nodes $\implies$ non-linear interaction.
  \item \textbf{Paths = 0 (Pruned Noise)}: Covariate completely severed from computation graph.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}

## Local Explainability via Polyhedral ReLU Activation Regions

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Local GLM Theorem (JSM 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Piecewise-linear activations partition $\mathbb{R}^p$ into polyhedral activation regions $\mathcal{P}_1, \dots, \mathcal{P}_M$.
  \item Within each local region $\mathcal{P}_m$, the active network reduces to an exact \textbf{local GLM}:
  \small
  $$\zeta(\mathbf{x}) = \beta_0(\mathbf{x}_i) + \sum_{j=1}^p \beta_j(\mathbf{x}_i) x_j$$
  $$\boldsymbol{\beta}(\mathbf{x}_i) = \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \zeta(\mathbf{x})\big|_{\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x}_i}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Exact Gradients}: Evaluated via analytical backpropagation (zero perturbation error).
  \item \textbf{Credible Intervals}: Draws $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma^*)$ yield exact posterior intervals for respondent sensitivities.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/jsm_polyhedral_regions.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Variational Inference & Protection Against Cold Posteriors

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Variational ELBO at True $T = 1.0$:}
\small
$$\text{ELBO}(q) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}_{q}[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)] - \text{KL}(q \parallel p)$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Why Explicit Error Scale $\sigma^2$ Matters (Wenzel et al., 2020):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Omitting residual noise scale $\sigma^2$ artificially rescales likelihood ($T = \sigma^2 \neq 1$), mis-calibrating spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
  \item In \texttt{lbbnn\_net(sigma = ...)}, calibrated $\sigma^2$ grounds log-likelihood sensitivities on the true Bayesian scale.
  \item Calibrates both feature inclusion probabilities $\alpha_k$ and DP sensitivities $f_i$.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/jsm_variational_elbo.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

# PART II: Track 1 — Unit-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors & Formal Differential Privacy

## Unit-Weighted Variational Pseudo-Posteriors (Savitsky & Toth, 2016)

\vspace{0.2em}
Equipping each unit $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ with a non-negative weight $u_i \ge 0$ defines the pseudo-posterior:
\small
$$p_{\mathbf{u}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}) \propto p(\theta) \prod_{i=1}^n f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)^{u_i}$$
$$\text{ELBO}(q; \mathbf{u}) = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \, \mathbb{E}_{q(\theta)}\!\left[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)\right] - \text{KL}\big(q(\theta) \parallel p(\theta)\big)$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{1. Survey Sampling Weights ($u_i = \tilde{w}_i$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Normalized to sample size $n$: $\tilde{w}_i = w_i \frac{n}{\sum w_j}$.
  \item Setting \texttt{normalize\_weights = TRUE} ensures $\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$ does not overpower spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
  \item Corrects informative sampling selection bias.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{2. Differential Privacy Weights ($u_i = \alpha_i$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Unnormalized weights: $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$.
  \item Setting \texttt{normalize\_weights = FALSE} ensures $\sum \alpha_i \le n$.
  \item Downweights high-sensitivity tail outliers and contracts the pseudo-posterior toward the prior.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Track 1A — Informative Survey Sampling Setup & Automated Noise Pruning

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 2,000, p = 4$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{True Non-Linear DGP}:
  \small
  $$Y_i = 2 X_{1i} + 1.5 \sin(\pi X_{2i}) + 0.8 X_{1i} X_{2i} + \varepsilon_i$$
  \normalsize
  where $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.4^2)$, and $X_3, X_4 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ are pure noise.
  \item \textbf{Informative Selection Mechanism}:
  \small
  $$\pi_i = \text{logit}^{-1}(-1.0 + 1.2 Y_i)$$
  \normalsize
  Draws $n = 737$ units favoring high $Y_i$.
  \item Unweighted sample mean is \textbf{+2.009} (True population mean: \textbf{0.000}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Track 1B — Why Unweighted Neural Networks Fail Differential Privacy

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Probabilistic Differential Privacy (Savitsky, Williams \& Hu, 2022):}
\small
$$\sup_{\theta \in \Theta_\delta} \left|\log \frac{q_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y})}{q_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}')}\right| \le \epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2 \Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}, \qquad \Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s, i} |\alpha_i \log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta^{(s)})|$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{The Quadratic Exposure Dilemma in Gaussian Regression:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Pointwise Gaussian log-likelihood grows quadratically with the residual:
  $$|\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)| \propto \frac{(y_i - \mu_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i))^2}{2\sigma^2}$$
  \item In skewed survey microdata (wages, financial expenditures), extreme outliers drive unweighted sensitivity $\Delta \to \infty$ and privacy budget $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} \to \infty$.
  \item Naive gradient clipping distorts the mean and destroys the variance structure of official statistics.
\end{itemize}

## Track 1B — The Two-Pass Surgical Downweighting Pipeline (`fit_dp_lbbnn`)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.72, every node/.style={scale=0.72, font=\sffamily}]
  \node[rectangle, draw=blue!80, fill=blue!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.4cm, align=center] (p1) at (0, 0) {\textbf{Pass 1}\\[2pt]Unweighted Fit\\[2pt]($u_i = 1$)};
  \node[rectangle, draw=orange!80, fill=orange!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.5cm, align=center] (risk) at (3.4, 0) {\textbf{Extract Risk}\\[2pt]$S \times n$ Matrix $L_{s,i}$\\[2pt]$f_i = \max_s |L_{s,i}|$};
  \node[rectangle, draw=purple!80, fill=purple!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.6cm, align=center] (weight) at (7.0, 0) {\textbf{Surgical Weights}\\[2pt]Smooth $\alpha_i^{\text{raw}}$\\[2pt]Zero Tail Outliers};
  \node[rectangle, draw=green!70!black, fill=green!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.4cm, align=center] (p2) at (10.6, 0) {\textbf{Pass 2}\\[2pt]$\alpha$-Weighted Fit\\[2pt]$\Delta_{\alpha} \le M_{\text{thresh}}$};
  \node[rectangle, draw=red!80, fill=red!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.2cm, align=center] (synth) at (14.0, 0) {\textbf{Synthesis}\\[2pt]$(\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}}, \delta)$-PDP Microdata};
  
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (p1) -- (risk);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (risk) -- (weight);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (weight) -- (p2);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (p2) -- (synth);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Monotone Surgical Truncation Formula:}
$$\alpha_i = \min\!\left(\alpha_i^{\text{raw}}, \, \frac{M_{\text{thresh}}}{f_i}\right), \qquad \alpha_i = 0 \quad \text{if } f_i > 3 M_{\text{thresh}}$$
Guarantees local Lipschitz bound $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s,i} |\alpha_i L_{s,i}^{(2)}| \le M_{\text{thresh}}$ and bounded privacy $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}$.

# PART III: Track 2 — Combining Probability & Non-Probability Samples

## The Big Data Paradox in Convenience Samples (Meng, 2018)

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Non-Probability Selection Dilemma:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item In convenience/opt-in samples $S_c$, sample inclusion $I_{ci} \in \{0, 1\}$ is non-random and driven by unobserved self-selection mechanisms.
  \item \textbf{Meng's Law of Large Populations (2018)}:
  $$\text{Bias}(\bar{y}_c) = \frac{\text{Cov}_U(I_c, Y)}{\bar{\pi}_c} = \rho_{I_c, Y} \cdot \sigma_Y \cdot \sqrt{\frac{N - n_c}{n_c}}$$
  \item A tiny correlation $\rho_{I_c, Y} \neq 0$ creates selection bias that scales with $\sqrt{N}$.
  \item Merely increasing convenience sample size $n_c$ shrinks variance around a severely biased estimate (the Big Data Paradox).
\end{itemize}

## The Identification Barrier & The Conditioning Trick (Beresovsky et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Identification Barrier:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item We observe covariates $\mathbf{x}_i$ only on convenience sample $S_c$ (unknown $\pi_{ci}$) and reference survey $S_r$ (known design probability $\pi_{ri}$), never on $U \setminus (S_c \cup S_r)$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{The Conditioning Trick:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Pool $S_c$ and $S_r$ into a combined sample $S$, and model membership indicator $D_i = \mathbb{I}(i \in S_c)$:
  $$\pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}} = \mathbb{P}(D_i = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i, i \in S) = \frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$$
  \item The known reference probability $\pi_{ri}$ acts as an \textbf{exact structural offset}, anchoring neural network logits $\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)$ to the true population scale.
\end{itemize}

## The Five Sample Combination Formulations (Beresovsky et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.35}
\footnotesize
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Estimator} & \textbf{Sample Domain} & \textbf{Target Indicator} & \textbf{Composite Probability $\pi_{zi}$} \\
\midrule
\texttt{STACK} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Unlinked) & $I_{zi} = D_i$ (sample source) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ \\[4pt]
\texttt{LINK1} & $S_c \cup (S_r \setminus S_c)$ & $I_{zi} = I_{ci}$ (deduplicated) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri} - \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}}$ \\[4pt]
\texttt{LINK2} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Linked Stacked) & $I_{zi} = D_i + (1-D_i)I_{ci}$ & $\frac{\pi_{ci}(1 + \pi_{ri})}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ \\[4pt]
\texttt{MIP} & Missing Information & $\tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} = D_i + (1-D_i)\tilde{p}_i$ & Bridges \texttt{STACK} and \texttt{LINK2} \\[4pt]
\texttt{PSEUDO} & Survey Weighted & Score: $\nabla \ell_{\text{pseudo}} = 0$ & Design-weighted: $\sum_{S_r} \pi_{ri}^{-1}\text{softplus}(\eta_i)$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

## How `MIP` Bridges `STACK` and `LINK2` vs. Why `PSEUDO` Explodes

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Louis's (1982) Missing Information Principle (\texttt{MIP}):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Imputes linkage expectations on unlinked reference units:
  $$\tilde{p}_i = p_{\text{link}} I_{ci} + (1 - p_{\text{link}})\text{sg}(\pi_{ci}), \qquad \tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} = D_i + (1 - D_i)\tilde{p}_i$$
  \item Continuously bridges unlinked \texttt{STACK} ($p_{\text{link}} = 0$) and deterministically linked \texttt{LINK2} ($p_{\text{link}} = 1$).
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{The Pseudo-Likelihood (\texttt{PSEUDO}) Breakdown:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{PSEUDO} scores reference units with inverse design weights $\pi_{ri}^{-1}$.
  \item Under low common support (where $\pi_{ci} \gg 0$ but $\pi_{ri} \approx 0$), weights $\pi_{ri}^{-1} \to \infty$, causing loss gradients and parameter variance to explode.
\end{itemize}

## Study 0 — Exact Linear Baseline Monte Carlo ($R = 20$, Visual Benchmark)

\includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{figures/track2_study0_rmse_bars.pdf}

\textbf{Empirical Findings}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Efficiency Hierarchy}: $\text{LINK2} \succ \text{LINK1} \succ \text{STACK} \succ \text{PSEUDO}$.
  \item \textbf{Pseudo-Likelihood Breakdown}: Under low common support, \texttt{GLM-PSEUDO} explodes to $\text{RMSE} = 1.015$, while composite likelihoods and \texttt{LBBNN} remain bounded ($\text{RMSE} \approx 0.13\text{--}0.17$).
  \item \textbf{LBBNN Agreement}: On linear truth, \texttt{LBBNN} matches parametric GLM efficiency ($\text{RMSE} = 0.231$ vs. $0.240$).
\end{itemize}

## Study 1 — Automated Confounder Selection & Noise Pruning ($p = 6$)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.42\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 5,000, p = 6$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Confounders}: $X_1, X_2$ drive both propensity $\pi_{ci}$ and outcome $Y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Outcome-Only}: $X_3$ drives $Y_i$ but uncorrelated with selection $I_c$.
  \item \textbf{Pure Noise}: $X_4, X_5, X_6 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Why Variable Selection Matters}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Including non-propensity predictors $X_3\text{--}X_6$ inflates H\'{a}jek weight variance without reducing confounding bias.
  \item \texttt{LBBNN} automatically prunes them.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

# PART IV: Unified Software Architecture & Synthesis

## Unified `LBBNN` Architecture Across Track 1 & Track 2

\vspace{0.1em}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.10}
\scriptsize
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{p{3.6cm}p{2.6cm}p{7.0cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Function / Module} & \textbf{Operational Track} & \textbf{Description \& Statistical Role} \\
\midrule
\texttt{get\_dataloaders()} & Track 1 \& 2 & Handles non-trainable weights $u_i \ge 0$, normalization, and multi-targets. \\
\texttt{lbbnn\_net(sigma, ...)} & Track 1 \& 2 & ELBO likelihood scaling by error variance $\sigma^2$ (cold-posterior protection). \\
\texttt{loglik\_contributions()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Computes $S \times n$ record-level log-likelihood contributions $L_{s, i}$. \\
\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Two-pass monotone surgical downweighting with Lipschitz bound $\Delta_{\alpha}$. \\
\texttt{sample\_synthetic\_lbbnn()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Generates $(\epsilon, \delta)$-DP synthetic microdata via post-processing theorem. \\
\midrule
\texttt{nll\_link1()} / \texttt{nll\_link2()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Composite Bernoulli NLL on singly matched and matched-pair samples. \\
\texttt{make\_nll\_mip(p\_link)} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Factory producing composite NLL under Missing Information Principle. \\
\texttt{nll\_stack()} / \texttt{nll\_pseudo()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Stacked pooled sample NLL and survey design-weighted pseudo-NLL. \\
\texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Formats covariates and targets for any of the 5 estimation methods. \\
\texttt{hajek\_estimate()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Computes self-normalizing H\'{a}jek estimator $\sum w_i y_i / \sum w_i$ with $w_i = \hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1}$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

## Key Takeaways & Synthesis for Official Statistics

\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Survey-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors (Track 1A)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Normalizing survey weights to sample size ($\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$) + calibrated observation noise $\sigma^2$ prevents likelihood mis-scaling ($T \neq 1$) and protects spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
      \item \texttt{LBBNN} achieves 5x lower population RMSE than classical H\'{a}jek weighting under informative sampling while pruning irrelevant covariates.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Two-Pass $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PDP Microdata Synthesis (Track 1B)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Monotone surgical downweighting (\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn}) eliminates disclosure risk from extreme tail outliers ($\alpha_i = 0$) while preserving high utility ($\alpha_i \in [0.34, 0.85]$) on normal records.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Composite Non-Probability Sample Integration (Track 2)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Conditioning on pooled sample inclusion $S_c \cup S_r$ allows known design probabilities $\pi_{ri}$ to anchor neural network logits to the true population scale.
      \item Composite Bernoulli likelihoods (\texttt{LINK2}, \texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{MIP}, \texttt{STACK}) bound loss gradients and prevent the catastrophic effective sample size collapse (\texttt{Kish ESS} $< 7$) of pseudo-likelihood under low common support.
    \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
